pages.title: X-ray Diffractometer
pages.text: X-rays scattered by a crystal's planes of atoms reinforce only at angles that fit the spacing between them. Find the angle, and you know the lattice - and how to cut it.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Set the tube voltage above copper's K-edge (8.98 kV) so it gives its Kα line (λ = 1.5406 Å), then the detector angle 2θ so that nλ = 2d·sin θ for the crystal's lattice spacing d. The sample comes back with a $(item)Laue Pattern$() and Insight. Keep the anode under 2.2 kW.

pages.name: X-ray Diffractometer
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Calcite, Fluorite Boule, Garnet Boule, Laue Pattern, Moissanite, Quartz, Sapphire Boule, Silicon Boule.
A photographic plate exposed to X-rays scattered by a crystal: a pattern of spots that shows how its lattice planes lie. Cut along them.$(br2)Made in $(item)X-ray Diffractometer$().
